content: FastAPI official docs on BackgroundTasks: tasks run after the response; the callable can be async def or plain def (Starlette runs sync ones in its threadpool via run_in_threadpool); docs explicitly warn heavy background computation belongs in a separate tool (Celery with Redis/RabbitMQ) when it need not share the app process. For this project the app MUST NOT share process memory with the triggered scripts anyway (they are existing standalone CLIs), so a lightweight threadpool-based runner inside the API process is appropriate; Celery-class infrastructure is unjustified for one user.
